result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.second_order_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute the second order centrality for nodes in the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L14727-L14907){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.second_order_centrality(attr_name=None, return_dict=False) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Second order centrality measures the standard deviation of return times to a node in a perpetual random walk on the graph. Lower values indicate higher centrality, as nodes with lower return time variance are more centrally positioned in the network structure. This metric is particularly useful for identifying nodes that are consistently reached in random walks, indicating their importance in network flow and connectivity patterns. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of node attribute to store centrality values. If `None`, uses `second_order_centrality`. Only used when `return_dict=False`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns dict mapping node IDs to centrality values. If `False`, stores values in graph and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict or Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=True`: dictionary mapping node ID to centrality value. If `return_dict=False`: self (for method chaining). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If either: (1) the graph is directed (algorithm only works for undirected graphs), (2) the graph is empty, or (3) the graph is not connected. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} **Algorithm Overview:** The algorithm implements the analytical solution from Kermarrec et al. (2011) based on Metropolis-Hastings random walks: 1. Balance the graph by adding self-loops to equalize in-degrees 2. Create transition probability matrix `P` 3. For each node `i`, solve the linear system: `(I - Q_i) * M[:, i] = 1` where `Q_i` is `P` with column `i` zeroed 4. Compute centrality as: `sqrt(2 * sum(M[:, i]) - n * (n + 1))` **Complexity:** - Time: `O(n³)` due to solving `n` linear systems of size `n×n` - Space: `O(n²)` for storing matrices **Interpretation:** - **Lower values** = **higher centrality** (more central nodes) - Values represent consistency of return times in random walks - Captures both direct and indirect influence through network structure - Complements first-order metrics like degree or betweenness **Current Limitation:** - Only supports unweighted graphs (all edges treated equally) ## Examples {.doc-examples} Identify central nodes in a path graph (lower values = higher centrality): ::: {#79a80ae4 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec # Create a simple path: 0 - 1 - 2 - 3 - 4 graph = ec.Graph() for i in range(5): graph.add_node(label=str(i)) for i in range(4): graph.add_edge(str(i), str(i+1)) soc = graph.second_order_centrality(return_dict=True) # Middle nodes have lower values (higher centrality) # Note: keys are node IDs, not labels most_central_id = min(soc, key=soc.get) most_central_label = graph.get_label_from_id(most_central_id) # Returns '2' - the most central node (middle of path) most_central_label # Returns the centrality value for the most central node soc[most_central_id] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 4.47213595499958 ``` ::: ::: Compare centrality across different graph structures: ::: {#e838906d .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Star graph: center should be most central star = ec.Graph() star.add_node(label='center') for i in range(5): star.add_node(label=f'leaf_{i}') star.add_edge('center', f'leaf_{i}') star_soc = star.second_order_centrality(return_dict=True) center_id = star.get_id_from_label('center') leaf_id = star.get_id_from_label('leaf_0') # Lower value = more central (center node) star_soc[center_id] # Higher value = less central (leaf node) star_soc[leaf_id] # Complete graph: all nodes equally central complete = ec.Graph() for i in range(4): complete.add_node(label=str(i)) for i in range(4): for j in range(i+1, 4): complete.add_edge(str(i), str(j)) complete_soc = complete.second_order_centrality(return_dict=True) vals = list(complete_soc.values()) # Returns True - all nodes in complete graph are equally central all(abs(v - vals[0]) < 0.01 for v in vals) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` True ``` ::: ::: Store centrality as node attribute for later analysis: ::: {#52203c48 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label='A') .add_node(label='B') .add_node(label='C') .add_node(label='D') .add_edge('A', 'B') .add_edge('B', 'C') .add_edge('C', 'D') ) # Store with custom attribute name graph.second_order_centrality(attr_name='soc') # Verify it was computed has_soc = any('soc' in str(c) for c in graph._computations) # Returns True if second order centrality was computed has_soc ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` True ``` ::: :::
